id_and_class.summary: Holmgren proposes that conscious experience is grainy, built from discrete ‘atomic feels’, each the actualization of a small, brief, localized microprocess in the brain arising out of a continuous natural world. Clusters of these feels, stored as memory engrams, become concepts and abstract thought. He places the view inside an evolutionary framework and a Multi-Aspect Monism that refuses to reduce consciousness to any single science.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a succession of discrete atomic feels, each corresponding to one short-lived, localized brain microprocess. Large numbers of these feels, ordered in rich spectra of qualities, are all there is to build knowledge from.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Each feel is the actualization of a brain microprocess, so mind and brain are aspects of one natural process. Holmgren holds that this process must be understood from scientific, cultural, and spiritual perspectives together.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Emergence of discrete feels from continuous brain processes; Holmgren does not specify weak or strong
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Consciousness has an objective pole driven by the senses and a subjective pole driven by memory engrams that feed imagination, planning, and reflection. The two poles depend on each other.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are feels and their distributions in conceptual spaces, and they replace traditional universals. They are generated inside brains, so there are no light-qualia anywhere except in living organisms.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A continuous natural world, brain microprocesses, discrete atomic feels, memory engrams, and conceptual spaces; possibly astrocytes as part of the substrate.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: All knowledge comes through conscious experience, so Holmgren starts from first-person phenomenology, such as seeing rotating light voxels on waking in a dark room, and links it to neuroscience.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Atomic feels are the basic units, each with a precise location and brief duration. They cluster into concepts stored as engrams, and these build up layers of abstraction.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Memory, Conceptual thought, Perception across all sensory modalities, Emotion
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The graininess principle: experience is discrete while nature is continuous. Brain microprocesses switch on and off, and each actualization yields one atomic feel.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness arrives in rapid discrete bursts actualized out of continuous brain activity, which Holmgren links to brain update rates of about 50–60 Hz in humans and faster in birds.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Each feel has a precise location in the brain; distributed, holistic brain circuits may coordinate their synchronization and actualization.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conscious experience evolved to support reliable interaction with a continuous natural world, giving organisms the fine resolution needed for survival.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The brain integrates many atomic feels into coherent experiences; Holmgren sees the contrast between continuous nature and discrete experience as the source of the binding problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Feels cluster into stable patterns in conceptual space, stored as memory engrams, which allow categorization and higher-order thought.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Atomic feels were selected for survival-critical resolution, and evolution later favoured abstraction and culture. Holmgren recasts Dobzhansky's dictum as ‘Everything in life makes sense in the light of evolution’.
core_claims_and_evidence: On waking in a dark room, Holmgren reports seeing rotating light voxels, which he takes as direct evidence that visual consciousness is grainy.
Similar atomic-feel patterns appear in auditory experience and abstract cognition, so graininess holds for all modalities.
The persistence of atomic feels across individuals and cultures, along with species differences in brain update rates, points to a conserved evolutionary substrate.
Concepts are stable clusters of feels stored in memory engrams of the kind identified by Tonegawa and colleagues.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological (first-person observation), with supporting neuroscience and evolutionary argument

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Self-observation of visual experience on waking in darkness, auditory experiments, and comparison of brain update rates across species.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The central evidence is Holmgren's own introspective report, which others may not share or may explain differently. Multi-Aspect Monism adds cultural and spiritual aspects to the ontology without saying how they relate to brain microprocesses.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The neural substrate is left open, with engrams, astrocytes, and distributed circuits offered only as candidates. It is unclear what makes a microprocess's actualization felt at all.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Holmgren draws on Whitehead's process philosophy while calling his view an evolutionary, brain-based theory; pairing a Whiteheadian ontology of feeling with a materialist placement leaves some tension about whether feels are basic to nature or produced by brains.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since each atomic feel is the actualization of a brain microprocess, conscious experience depends on a living brain and does not outlast it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Holmgren grounds consciousness in evolution, yet his Multi-Aspect Monism keeps spiritual aspects in view without spelling out any cosmic purpose.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Holmgren’s Grainy, Atomic Feels, Jan Holmgren (Landscape of Consciousness entry)
